sources.quote: Our current deployment will include our remaining 1.4 million Ohio customers and is expected to wrap up in 2027.
sources.searcher_note: FirstEnergy statement quoted by local TV: 1.4M Ohio customers still awaiting smart meters, rollout ends 2027; story is about the $28.29 manual-read opt-out fee. Date from page metadata.

sources.quote: Grid Mod II will build on these efforts by deploying an additional 1.4 million smart meters
sources.searcher_note: Company release: 715,000+ Ohio smart meters under Grid Mod I (2020-22); phase II of 1.4M begins April 2025, ends 2027. Supports the lead's 'late, not refused' caveat for Ohio.

sources.quote: By 2026, we expect to have installed smart meters for nearly 80% of customers across our service territory.
sources.searcher_note: Company-wide smart meter target; implies roughly 20% of FirstEnergy customers still without smart meters in 2026.

sources.quote: the Commission initiated an investigation into PE's meter reading practices, estimations of bills, and its compliance with its tariffs based on the filing of several formal complaints
sources.searcher_note: PDF. Case No. 9329 (April 2013): MD PSC probe of Potomac Edison's hand meter-reading frequency and estimated bills; PE tariff is bi-monthly reading. Background, not a 2024 count.

sources.quote: Pepco and DPL have finished deploying smart meters with the final totals for each company being 560,851 and 211,115 smart meters, respectively.
sources.searcher_note: PDF. Lists smart-grid approvals for BGE, Pepco, DPL and SMECO only, all finished by 2018; Potomac Edison is absent from the list. Supports the in-state comparison, does not name PE.

sources.quote: now available because the smart meter rollout is complete
sources.searcher_note: Possible disagreement: energy-shopping site says Potomac Edison's (Maryland) smart meter rollout is complete; same page also says 'Potomac Edison installs a new advanced meter for free as part of enrollment' in a 2026 TOU pilot. Date is dateModified; datePublished 2014-11-13.

notes: No source found that reports FirstEnergy's hand-read share, the 2.26M count, or the ~27% of US hand-read meters. What exists: FirstEnergy's own statements that Ohio's 1.4M remaining meters get smart meters 2025-2027 and a company-wide 80%-by-2026 target; MD PSC reports showing every other Maryland IOU finished AMI by 2018 while Potomac Edison had no approved smart-grid case; MD PSC 2013 probe of PE hand meter reading. No West Virginia AMI plan for Mon Power/Potomac Edison found in 2026 rate-case coverage (Dominion Post 2026-03-09, Utility Dive 2026-05-19 checked; neither mentions meters). Also seen: StopPATH WV advocacy blog (2013-12-29, https://stoppathwv.com/stoppath-wv-blog/potomac-edisonmon-power-billing-meter-reading-investigation-evidentiary-hearing) on the WV PSC general investigation of Mon Power/Potomac Edison meter reading, quote verified: "AEP didn't have the same problems because their meter reading is automated and is a different process." CallMePower's 'rollout is complete' line is unsourced and conflicts with its own 'installs a new advanced meter' line.
